{"name":"pr4c/gvar-deformation","commit":{"sha":"692a44e38d0a58888213a49cc41640f33a549ab1","node_id":"C_kwDOAORW-9oAKDY5MmE0NGUzOGQwYTU4ODg4MjEzYTQ5Y2M0MTY0MGYzM2E1NDlhYjE","commit":{"author":{"name":"Benedikt Stebner","email":"Gillibald@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-06-12T14:45:15Z"},"committer":{"name":"Benedikt Stebner","email":"Gillibald@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-09-29T13:47:41Z"},"message":"Bound gvar packed-point and packed-delta reads to their tuple data

The packed readers indexed entry bytes with no validation of
dataOffsetFromEntryStart or tupleDataSize: an over-run past the entry
threw out of TryApplyDeltas and blanked the whole glyph, while an
over-run inside the entry silently consumed the next tuple bytes and
produced wrong deltas. Reads are now sandboxed per tuple - the data
window is clamped to the entry, both readers are bounded Try-methods,
and a tuple whose streams over-run is skipped to its declared end so
the remaining tuples still apply (worst case the outline renders
undeformed instead of blank). Truncated tuple headers stop header
processing, keeping whatever earlier tuples
